\begin{lstlisting}[language={},basicstyle=\ttfamily\scriptsize,breaklines=true]
// Generated by LeanFM from the message types of the protocol; regenerate it rather than editing.
syntax = "proto3";

package sign_in;

// The browser asks the app to sign in; return_to is where to go afterwards.
message Start {
  string return_to = 1;
}

// The app sends the browser to the identity provider. state is the session's key: it comes back on the callback and is how the app tells concurrent sign-ins apart. code_challenge is PKCE's S256 hash of a verifier only the app knows.
message RedirectToIdp {
  string state = 1;
  string client_id = 2;
  string redirect_uri = 3;
  string code_challenge = 4;
}

// The browser follows the redirect: the same parameters, as a GET on the provider.
message Authorize {
  string state = 1;
  string client_id = 2;
  string redirect_uri = 3;
  string code_challenge = 4;
}

message LoginPage {
}

// The person signs in at the provider; the password is a secret, never logged.
message Credentials {
  string username = 1;
  string password_secr = 2;
  string state = 3;
}

// The provider sends the browser back to the app with a one-time code.
message RedirectBack {
  string state = 1;
  string code = 2;
}

// Or the provider sends the browser back with an error, such as access_denied.
message DeniedBack {
  string state = 1;
  string error = 2;
}

// The browser follows the redirect to the app's callback with the code.
message Callback {
  string state = 1;
  string code = 2;
}

// Or it follows the error redirect to the same callback route.
message ErrorCallback {
  string state = 1;
  string error = 2;
}

// The app exchanges the code at the provider, proving it holds the PKCE verifier.
message ExchangeCode {
  string code = 1;
  string redirect_uri = 2;
  string client_id = 3;
  string code_verifier_secr = 4;
}

// The tokens are secrets, never logged.
message Tokens {
  string access_token_secr = 1;
  uint64 expires_in = 2;
}

// Signed in: the app sends the browser on to where it started.
message SignedIn {
  string return_to = 1;
}

message BadCode {
}

message SignInFailed {
}

// The event envelope: every event of the protocol, as it is carried and logged. Integers travel
// as decimal strings in JSON (the protobuf JSON mapping), so nanosecond timestamps stay exact.
message Event {
  uint64 ts = 1;        // nanoseconds; unique in its stream, and its identity
  string id = 2;        // the event's name, in a log that names events
  string session = 3;   // the session, or its key's value when the sessions block names one
  string from = 4;      // the sending actor: Role, or Role/instance
  string to = 5;        // the receiving actor
  string label = 6;
  string cause = 7;     // the id or ts of the event this one answers
  string prev = 8;      // the id or ts of the previous event the same actor sent
  uint64 sent_at = 9;   // the sender's clock when it sent, ns; compared only with that clock
  uint64 received_at = 10; // the receiver's clock when it received, ns
  oneof payload {
    Start start = 11;
    RedirectToIdp redirect_to_idp = 12;
    Authorize authorize = 13;
    LoginPage login_page = 14;
    Credentials credentials = 15;
    RedirectBack redirect_back = 16;
    Callback callback = 17;
    ExchangeCode exchange_code = 18;
    Tokens tokens = 19;
    SignedIn signed_in = 20;
    BadCode bad_code = 21;
    SignInFailed sign_in_failed = 22;
    DeniedBack denied_back = 23;
    ErrorCallback error_callback = 24;
  }
}
\end{lstlisting}
